ruledBy: Astra editorial review, adopted as Al's ruling (his instruction, 2026-09-05; veto list: none)
note: KEEP and FIX (fixed wording) are kept. KILL is held as `unruled`, NOT rejected — Al ruled that explicitly, so no downstream step may treat a KILL as struck. New-lines CSV rows are kept with source astra-new. astraTime is Astra's own visual reading of the hour and does not override the photograph's rotation slot.

kept.text: Your jacket knows better than your eyes.
kept.fixedFrom: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.

kept.text: You dressed by looking out the window again.
The bike is ready. Your ears are lodging objections.

unruled.text: Not one cloud, not one degree: a Highveld winter morning doing both at once.
unruled.reason: R1/R7 fail: condition inventory and regional label.

unruled.text: Blue overhead, ice in the air: he is dressed for the truth, not the view.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: captions sky, ice and clothing.

kept.text: Your alarm never checks what it's sending you into.
Up you get. The socks won't find themselves.

unruled.text: The hadeda has landed on frost and is already drafting a complaint.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the bird landing on frost.

unruled.text: Frost on the lawn and the morning alarm has just landed, feathers and all.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: frost-and-bird inventory.

unruled.text: The first bird down this morning found the grass crunchy and said so.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the pictured bird's arrival.

kept.text: Your face would also like a turn in the sun.
kept.fixedFrom: Sun on your back, freezer on your face.

kept.text: Your jacket was right to insist on coming.
Going out? The glass has given you enough of a look.

unruled.text: Full sun, visible breath: the Karoo running both seasons before lunch.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: inventories sunshine and breath.

unruled.text: That wall holds the morning's heat by ten and he knows exactly where to lean.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains why the pictured man leans there.

kept.text: The school run starts with negotiating the car doors.
Everyone's ready. Nobody has warm hands.

unruled.text: Breath like smoke, frost on the glass, sun already out: Highveld school run.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: picture inventory and regional shorthand.

unruled.text: The bakkie iced over under a completely clear sky, which is exactly how it works.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: meteorology lesson, no human turn.

unruled.text: The sun is up and doing its best; the frost is unconvinced so far.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: weather dialogue merely narrates the frost.

kept.text: The dog can hear visitors from in here perfectly well.
Last check of the gate. With all your clothes on.

unruled.text: Frost already forming and the sun barely down: tonight means business.
unruled.reason: R1 fail: repeats the condition and announces seriousness.

unruled.text: Even the guard dog's breath is showing, and the stars are not even out yet.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates breath and the sky.

unruled.text: A clear dusk on the Highveld is just the frost clearing its throat.
unruled.reason: R1/R7 fail: regional weather metaphor without a human consequence.

kept.text: You'll need those towels to bend before you fold them.
Bring the washing in. Then thaw your fingers.

unruled.text: The towels went out damp and are coming in as boards.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: captions the stiff towels.

unruled.text: Sunset is doing the colours; the frost is already doing the towels.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: assigns jobs to sunset and visible frost.

unruled.text: That washing is not dry; it is preserved. Winter dusk works fast out here.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: preservation metaphor still describes the towels.

kept.text: Nobody's volunteering to fetch the extra chairs.
Sundowners, apparently. Make yours a mug.

unruled.text: Clear sky, sharp air, one fire bowl doing the work of a whole summer.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories sky, air and fire bowl.

unruled.text: The temperature dropped with the sun and the circle got tighter by exactly that much.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: narrates cooling and the pictured circle.

unruled.text: The evening turned cold the minute it turned beautiful, which is the usual trade.
unruled.reason: R2 fail: scenic trade-off copy suitable for a lodge advert.

kept.text: Spectating has become the harder sport tonight.
Kick-off soon. Feeling your toes would be useful.

unruled.text: A sky that clean means the field freezes before the floodlights even warm up.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: weather explanation attached to visible field.

unruled.text: Frost on the pitch an hour after sundown — whoever trains tonight earns it.
unruled.reason: R1 fail: condition report precedes a generic toughness compliment.

unruled.text: The blankets on the bench are not decoration; the touchline is minus something.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the visible blankets and touchline.

kept.text: You forgot something outside and remembered your duvet.
One look before bed. From this side of the glass.

unruled.text: The Southern Cross is out and the lawn has gone silver under it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: literal sky-and-lawn caption.

unruled.text: A sky this clean at night is beautiful, and it charges in degrees.
unruled.reason: R2 fail: scenic admiration with a price metaphor.

unruled.text: Stars that sharp come standard with air this cold — it is a package deal.
unruled.reason: R2/R7 fail: stock stargazing package-deal copy.

kept.text: Your second cup is mostly a hand-warming arrangement.
Bed can wait. The blanket has come with.

unruled.text: The blanket came outside because the sky was worth it, and it is.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: describes the blanket and endorses the view.

unruled.text: The cold is charging admission tonight and the sky is worth every degree.
unruled.reason: R1/R2 fail: condition opener followed by scenic salesmanship.

unruled.text: Steam off the mug, frost on the veld, stars on duty: Sunday closed properly.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories mug, frost and stars.

kept.text: The fire is the only thing out here allowed to take its jacket off.
Nobody's asking how long the meat takes tonight.
Another log. For the cook, apparently.

unruled.text: Braaiing in beanies under a hard clear sky: winter never cancelled anything here.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: beanie-and-braai caption becomes a boast.

unruled.text: The stars came out for the wors, and the frost came with them.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: decorates the pictured stars and braai.

kept.text: Your slippers deserve better than this early start.
The chores can wait. Your fingers called first.

unruled.text: Frost right up to the dam wall: the Karoo did its winter thing overnight.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: frost description and regional filler.

unruled.text: Not enough wind to turn one blade, which is why the frost got everything.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: explains a windmill and frost.

unruled.text: Pink sky, white veld: the desert runs both extremes before breakfast.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: colour inventory without a human turn.

kept.text: Bin day has added another layer to getting dressed.
The truck is coming. Find both gloves.

unruled.text: Bin day, and the frost got to them before the truck did.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the frosted bins through arrival order.

unruled.text: Even the bins iced over, which is the Winelands telling you to dress properly.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: explains pictured bins using a regional label.

unruled.text: The municipality collects at seven; the frost delivered at four.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: delivery metaphor still captions the frosted bins.

kept.text: You promised yourself a run, not enthusiasm.
Early start. An idea you had while still in bed.

unruled.text: Joburg winter dawn: the view is free; the air charges admission.
unruled.reason: R2/R7 fail: regional tourism line.

unruled.text: His breath is the only cloud between here and the Hillbrow Tower.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: breath and landmark description.

unruled.text: The city looks its best exactly when the air hurts most, which is unfair.
unruled.reason: R2 fail: scenic praise with a mild complaint attached.

kept.text: The alarm went off before the car was ready to wake.
School bags packed. Hands still defrosting.

unruled.text: The windscreen kept a record of last night and she is deleting it by hand.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: deletion metaphor narrates visible scraping.

unruled.text: Two beanies, one scraper, minus three: the school run starts before the car agrees.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: counts clothing and tools, invents a temperature.

unruled.text: The car spent the night outside under a clear sky and it shows, everywhere.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly explains the car's appearance.

kept.text: You're up early enough to regret it twice.
One lap of the block. Then we discuss breakfast.

unruled.text: Five guinea fowl crossing in single file: the frost has everyone walking carefully.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: counts and explains the pictured birds.

unruled.text: First traffic of the morning, and it walks and complains at the same time.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: bird traffic is the complete visual joke.

unruled.text: Frost on every lawn and the only ones out are wearing feathers.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes frost and birds.

kept.text: The best seat is the one you refuse to leave.
Plenty of room outside, if anyone asks why you stayed.

unruled.text: Full sun, brown grass, visible breath: the boerboel has found the warm wall.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: sun, grass, breath and dog inventory.

unruled.text: The sunny side of the wall is prime property, and it is taken.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: property metaphor describes the dog's position.

unruled.text: The lawn went beige weeks ago; the sky never got the memo.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: colours plus a borrowed memo joke.

kept.text: You signed up for running, not feeling your fingers.
Keep moving. Chatting is an indoor activity.

unruled.text: Half the field is steam before anyone has run a step.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes steam on the field.

unruled.text: Frost on the grass, steam off the field: winter running weather at its most honest.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories frost, steam and running.

unruled.text: Cold enough to see every breath, clear enough that nobody minds.
unruled.reason: R1/R2 fail: repeats conditions and invents universal approval.

kept.text: Your evening walk has developed a very short route.
Home already? Sensible pace.

unruled.text: The horses are doing their own weather report, one breath at a time.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the horses' breath.

unruled.text: The frost is back on the grass before the sun is even gone.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: describes frost and sunset.

unruled.text: Golden light, silver breath: a winter dusk doing both its tricks at once.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: colour-and-breath caption.

kept.text: Admire it from the couch; that's what windows are for.
Another cup. The view isn't going anywhere.

unruled.text: The window is frosting at the edges and the cat has the best seat for it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes the window and the cat.

unruled.text: That sunset is happening at two degrees, which is why it is watched from inside.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the viewpoint using an invented temperature.

unruled.text: Pink sky through cold glass: winter does its best work at a distance.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: scenic caption sells distance as comfort.

kept.text: One more shot. Then you can feel your fingers.
kept.fixedFrom: Free throws until the light or the temperature gives out, whichever is first.

kept.text: Your fingers would like a turn inside the pockets.
Last shot. You said that before you lost feeling.

unruled.text: Shorts and a beanie: half of her believes the sky, half believes the air.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the pictured clothing contrast.

unruled.text: Every shot comes with its own little cloud of breath tonight.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the pictured breath.

kept.text: Taking the bin out counts as your evening walk.
kept.fixedFrom: Taking the bin out counts as an expedition once the frost settles in.

kept.text: Taking the bin out should count towards your steps.
Shoes on this time. You've learnt.

unruled.text: The bin run is being done at speed tonight, and the sky knows why.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the visible bin trip.

unruled.text: Clear night, hard frost coming: even the bin trip earns a beanie.
unruled.reason: R1/R5 fail: condition inventory explains the beanie.

kept.text: Tomorrow's first appointment is with the windscreen.
Set the alarm earlier. The car won't.

unruled.text: Every windscreen on this street is white already, and it is not even late.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes the frosted cars.

unruled.text: The streetlights are warm-toned; nothing else out here is.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: contrasts lamp colour with the condition.

unruled.text: The frost is doing the rounds tonight and skipping nobody.
unruled.reason: R1 fail: weather has agency but nobody gains a consequence.

kept.text: Movie night starts early. Getting warm takes time.
kept.fixedFrom: Movie night moved up an hour the moment the frost showed up on the hedge.

kept.text: The remote can wait until your hand is out again.
Movie night. Nobody's voting for a trip to the shops.

unruled.text: Outside is glitter and minus three; inside is fleece and the remote.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories the entire indoor-outdoor contrast.

unruled.text: The frost got the garden; the family got the couch. Fair trade.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: restates the garden-and-couch composition.

kept.text: Your duvet has finally been invited on a date.
Stay another minute. Then we'll need another blanket.

unruled.text: Duvets in the bakkie, flask on the tailgate: the sky is worth the freeze tonight.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: prop inventory becomes a scenic endorsement.

unruled.text: Winter skies are the sharp ones — the cold is the price of that many stars.
unruled.reason: R2 fail: tourism copy sells stars against discomfort.

unruled.text: The heater is at home; the Milky Way is here; the duvet split the difference.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories the scene through a compromise metaphor.

kept.text: You can finish that conversation somewhere with walls.
Table outside? Your scarf would like to object.

unruled.text: Coats and coffees in full sun: winter in this city photographs like summer.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly describes how the photograph looks.

unruled.text: The sky says lunch outside; the scarves say make it a quick one.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: captions sky and scarves as competing instructions.

unruled.text: Not a cloud between the towers, and still nobody unbuttoned anything.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes sky and clothing.

kept.text: The jacket argument is holding up breakfast.
Have another spoonful. We're finding the other sleeve.

unruled.text: The jacket is going on because the window already said so.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the visible jacket being put on.

unruled.text: Porridge steaming, veld frosted: breakfast comes with a dress code today.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: breakfast-and-frost inventory with a dress-code label.

unruled.text: The face says no; the frost outside says absolutely yes.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: tells us what the face and frost mean.

kept.text: How many warm-ups were you planning on doing?
Boots packed. Still negotiating with the legs.

unruled.text: The frost only survives in the stand's shadow, and you can see the exact line.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly describes the visible frost boundary.

unruled.text: Blue sky, gold grass, white edges: a Highveld rugby morning in full kit.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: colour inventory and regional shorthand.

unruled.text: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
unruled.reason: R1/R2 fail: condition opener and picturesque sports-ground praise.
